overview: 2.Nh3 is an odd anti-Sicilian: the knight aims for f4 and keeps the f-pawn free, but it is awkward on h3. Black normally replies ...d5 or ...Nc6/...g6 and has a comfortable Sicilian set-up. The line is a surprise weapon with little theory.

white_ideas.idea: Play Nf4 and f4 ideas on the kingside

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian-type structure with a half-open c-file for Black

character.notes: A quiet sideline in which Black has easy development.

structure.notes: A Sicilian structure with the c-file half-open.

level.notes: Simple, but offers little to learn.

character.reason: A quiet sideline in which neither side faces early danger.

gambit.reason: Material is level and no pawn is offered.

soundness.reason: The knight is awkward but there is no tactical flaw.

level.reason: Not a good first repertoire choice since the knight is poorly placed.
